description: Frontend: surface product status in the admin. Add status to the Product type, an admin products API client call + query hook that reads the new GET /api/admin/products (so drafts are visible), and update AdminProducts.tsx with a status badge column, a per-row Publish/Unpublish button with a client-side required-field check mirroring the server guard, and an optional status field in the add/edit modal. Depends on FEAT-001 (the admin list endpoint, the status column, and the server publish guard must exist first).
steps: types.ts: in interface Product (web/src/types.ts) add `status?: 'draft' | 'published';` with a one-line comment (admin publish/unpublish; the public catalog returns only published, so storefront reads may treat an absent status as published).

queries.ts: in web/src/lib/queries.ts, pass `status` through normalizeProduct unchanged (it already spreads ...p). Add `useAdminProducts()` using queryKey ['admin-products'], staleTime 0, refetchOnWindowFocus true, queryFn calling fetchAdminProducts() and mapping through normalizeProduct so price/mrp/max_qty normalize consistently.

admin.ts (client): in web/src/lib/admin.ts add `export async function fetchAdminProducts(): Promise<import('../types').Product[]> { return (await api.get('/admin/products')).data.products as import('../types').Product[]; }` near the existing saveProduct/deleteProduct Products section.

AdminProducts.tsx source switch: change `const { data: prods = [], isLoading } = useProducts();` to the new `useAdminProducts()` (import it from '../../lib/queries') so draft products appear in the admin table. Keep useCategories() as-is.

AdminProducts.tsx FormState: add `status: 'draft' | 'published'` to the FormState interface and set it in toForm — `status: (p?.status as 'draft'|'published') || 'published'` (editing an existing row defaults to its current status; a brand-new add will be defaulted to draft by the server).

AdminProducts.tsx table: add a `Status` header (e.g. after the Stock column) and a matching badge cell per row reusing the stock-badge styling: `{p.status === 'published' ? 'Published' : 'Draft'}` (green published / gray draft). Bump the empty-state row colSpan to match the new column count.

AdminProducts.tsx Publish/Unpublish button: add a per-row button in the Action cell — label `🚀 Publish` when p.status !== 'published', `⏸ Unpublish` when published. On click call a helper `async function setStatus(p, next)`: if next === 'published', first run a client-side required-field check mirroring the server (name non-empty, price > 0, category non-empty, image non-empty) and if incomplete showToast an error listing what's missing (bilingual) and return WITHOUT calling the API; otherwise call `saveProduct('update', { id: p.id, name: p.name, price: p.price, mrp: p.mrp, category: p.category, image: p.image, status: next })`, then on success showToast (bilingual: published vs unpublished) and `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['admin-products'] })` plus `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['products'] })` so storefront caches refresh. Wrap in try/catch and show `apiError(e)` on a server 422.

AdminProducts.tsx modal (optional surface): add `status` into the save() payload (so the add/edit modal can also set it) and optionally a small Status select in the modal grid (Draft/Published). The primary control remains the row button; keep this minimal.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` in web type-checks (tsc -b) and produces a production build with no errors.
interface Product includes an optional status field; AdminProducts.tsx reads useAdminProducts() so draft products are listed.
The admin table shows a green Published / gray Draft badge per product.
Each row has a Publish/Unpublish button; clicking Publish on a product missing a required field shows an error toast and does NOT call the API; a server 422 is surfaced via apiError.
After a successful publish/unpublish the admin list and the storefront product query are invalidated.
verification: cd web; npm install (if node_modules missing); npm run build
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Files changed (all under 4astore-v2/web/src):

- types.ts: interface Product now has optional `status?: 'draft' | 'published'` with the storefront-treats-absent-as-published comment.

- lib/admin.ts: added `fetchAdminProducts()` (GET /admin/products -> data.products) in the Products section, right above saveProduct.

- lib/queries.ts: imported fetchAdminProducts and added `useAdminProducts()` (queryKey ['admin-products'], staleTime 0, refetchOnWindowFocus/refetchOnReconnect true, queryFn maps through the existing normalizeProduct). normalizeProduct already spreads ...p so status passes through unchanged; no change to normalizeProduct body was needed.

- pages/admin/AdminProducts.tsx: switched the list source from useProducts() to useAdminProducts() so DRAFTS appear. FormState gained `status: 'draft' | 'published'`; toForm sets `status: (p?.status as ...) || 'published'`. save() payload now includes `status: f.status`. Added a Status badge column (header after Stock; cell reuses stock-badge: stock-in=green Published / stock-out=gray Draft) and bumped the empty-state colSpan 10 -> 11. Added a per-row Publish/Unpublish button in the Action cell (green 🚀 Publish when not published, gray ⏸ Unpublish when published) driven by `setStatus(p, next)`: when publishing it runs a client-side required-field check mirroring the server guard (name non-empty, price > 0, category non-empty, image non-empty) and on miss shows a bilingual error toast ('Publish ke liye ye zaroori hain / Required to publish: ' + list, items like 'name / naam', 'price / keemat', 'category / category', 'image / photo') and returns WITHOUT calling the API; otherwise it POSTs saveProduct('update', {id,name,price,mrp,category,image,status}) (carries the guard fields in the same request), shows a bilingual success toast, and invalidates both ['admin-products'] and ['products']. try/catch surfaces a server 422 via apiError(e). Also added an optional Status select (Draft/Published) in the modal grid beside the Featured select.

VERIFICATION: cd web; npm install (node_modules was missing — installed 172 pkgs); npm run build => sitemap generated, `tsc -b` type-check clean, `vite build` produced the production bundle with NO errors (only the pre-existing >500kB chunk-size advisory). Acceptance criteria all met.
